The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Head-sha: `15058d6ff808951416948a1d83dcb99f120f8a02`

**Gate verdicts = the check-runs on this head:** 39 success, 7 skipped (opt-in and filtered lanes: Console Pin Gate, Dogfood shards, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke, and the re-fired Auto Label / Check PR Size), 2 failure — both are `Check Changeset` (the same job fired twice on this head, run 38328587521 and the re-run 38332224488), red by design on the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class and judged in ① below. Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, every Type Check lane, Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 1–6 and the card/branch/single-writer guards are green.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept sets and public surfaces the diff implies**

1. No file under `packages/spec` moves, so no accept set moves; no package `index` or export moves, so no public surface moves. Right. The `Clause-②: no` declaration with no direction arm matches, and the red job's own level-axis step read it the same way.
2. **The runtime authorization change in `assertMasterRowEditable`** (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts`): one line of code — the write-RLS leg now passes `masterGateCoversThisWrite: !delegatedWrite && this.declaresControlledByParent(rel.master)` to `computeRlsFilter`. Judged **exactly the class the ruling names, no wider**:
   - What the flag does, read at the head: `computeRlsFilter` hands it to `platformFloorYieldsToObjectWriteModel`, which fires only when the flag is set AND `masterGateCoversOperation` holds (update/delete; the hop asks `update`) AND `declaresControlledByParent(object)` holds for that master; what it then removes is `collected.filter(!isPlatformOwnershipFloorPolicy)` — the platform floor policies only, ahead of the #7665 derive-from-select branch, Layer 0 untouched, app-authored policies untouched. So only the platform floor yields; an app's own update RLS and the derive-from-select floor still run — the ruling's clause, as written.
   - `!delegatedWrite` is read off `opCtx.context.onBehalfOf`, the carrier shared by both passes of a delegated write, so a delegated write keeps both principals' floors — the ruling's second clause.
   - The predicate is the walk's own continue condition (`if (!this.declaresControlledByParent(masterObject)) break;` in `assertControlledByParentWrite`), so whenever the flag lifts the floor the walk proceeds to that master's own master gate on the same pass, or refuses on the cycle guard, the depth bound or a broken chain — none of those branches is in the diff. A master that governs its own rows never sets it: the single-level case is unchanged.
   - The newly admitted set is therefore the principals whom the hop's write-RLS leg refused on the platform floor ALONE: `org_member`-position principals who did not create the middle master, hold `update` on it, and whose root legs pass — which is exactly the set whose direct by-id update of the middle master is admitted under step 2.7 (same floor, same predicate, same root gate). That is the class the binding lifts the hard stop for: organization members who can already update that middle master by id. The object-permission leg, the record-sharing leg with its authored-widener defer, the root legs, the bulk path (which never reaches this method) and the read path are untouched.
   - The composition's other direction: the creator of a middle master that an app-authored update policy refuses was admitted at the hop (floor OR policy) and is now refused, as the direct update already refused them. A narrowing for that one class, inside the ruling ("judged by its own direct-write composition"; "an app's own update RLS still applies"), required by the fork-clause invariant, and disclosed in the changeset's "Also refused now" bullet. Right.
   - `security/explain` and the `sys_attachment` / `sys_comment` parent gates reach the same method through `checkControlledByParentWrite`, so they move with it; that is one composition, not a second widening. Right.
3. **Pins** — `controlled-by-parent-chain-middle-master.test.ts` (new): a real ObjectQL with the SQL driver, the real SecurityPlugin and SharingService middleware, `member_default` carrying the floor, principals holding `org_member`. The four ruled pins are present: pin 1 middle editable → admitted and the row changed, for update, insert and delete; pin 2 root not editable (readable, and unreadable) → refused naming `cbc_account`; pin 3 middle not editable → by the object grant, by an app-authored update policy, and that policy's creator case, with an open-quote control; pin 4 delegated writes keep both floors, agent-side and delegator-side, each beside an undelegated control. Every case asserts the quote's own by-id update next to the line writes — the fork clause's invariant, pinned case by case. Right. A new sibling file rather than `controlled-by-parent-chain.test.ts` is justified: that rig's principals hold no position, so the floor never binds there. The refusal-pin ablations (A2, A3a, A3b, A4) and A0 are on the PR body and report 6135392664; each maps to a refusal pin and none is missing; not re-run here (read-only).
4. `packages/verify/src/parent-write-reach.test.ts`: expectation flip only — `pwr_quote_line` contradicted → proven; summary proven 3 / contradicted 0 / held 135 / hardFailures 0; `detail-only` stays `ALL_REFUSED`. PR #23091 landed first (its file is on the merge base), so by the declared order (6132790096) this PR flips it. Right. `packages/cli/test/verify-parent-write-reach.test.ts` is untouched: its fixture is single-level (`vpw_contract` under `vpw_account`), verified at the head; nothing to flip. Right.
5. Docblocks: the `RlsFilterOptions.masterGateCoversThisWrite` call-site roster gains the chain hop, pointing at the leg's own bullet; the leg's bullet that read "A master that is itself a detail keeps its floor exactly as it does today" now states the ruling. Comments only; the roster of vouching call sites is complete again. Right.
6. Published prose — `packages/verify/README.md` (ships in the tarball) and `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` — judged sentence by sentence under the correction below.

**DELIBERATE CORRECTION — confirmed.** `Check Changeset` is red on this head because the PR edits `.changeset/15953-verify-parent-write-reach-family.md`, the pending release note of `@objectstack/verify` (minor) and `@objectstack/cli` (minor) that PR #23091 added and this PR did not. The gate's log names the file and the class ("DELIBERATE CORRECTION — your change may have made this PENDING release note false, and you rewrote it in the same stroke. Remedy: do NOT restore it — say so on the PR and get it confirmed"). The diff to that file is ONE sentence (line 19, one line added, one removed); nothing else in it moves, nothing is restored, renamed or deleted; no `skip-changeset` label is on the PR, correctly, since the note is a pending release. The same job ran its later steps past the red and they passed: ADR-0087 disposition (no declared-breaking changeset among the two it saw), no `major`, level axis read as clause-② no. This record is the written confirmation, sentence by sentence:

- **The changeset, line 19.** OLD: "Today's engine refuses every write to a detail two levels below its root master, even where the caller edits the middle master, so on an app that declares such a chain the family reports a contradiction and the run fails." **Made false by this PR:** at this head the hop judges the middle master by its own direct-write composition, so a caller who edits the middle master is admitted (pin 1; and `pwr_quote_line` proven with 0 contradictions in the family's own test), and such a chain no longer fails the run. NEW: "A detail two levels below its root master (a line under a quote under an account) is answered the same way: its write is admitted exactly when the caller holds the verb on the detail and may update the middle master directly, which also needs edit access to the root, and refused otherwise, so the family reports such a chain `proven`." **Truthful on this head:** "admitted exactly when … may update the middle master directly" is the fork-clause invariant the pins hold in every case (admitted: pin 1 and the pin-3 control; refused: root not editable, root not readable, middle grant missing, app policy refusing, the creator under that policy, both delegated cases — each beside a matching direct quote update); "which also needs edit access to the root" is true because the middle master's own by-id update runs its master gate on the root (pin 2 refuses there, naming `cbc_account`); "reports such a chain `proven`" is the flipped expectation in `parent-write-reach.test.ts`. Confirmed; do not restore.
- **`packages/verify/README.md`, the twin.** OLD: "Today's engine refuses every write to a detail two levels below its root master, even where the caller edits the middle master, so on an app that declares such a chain the family reports a contradiction and fails the run." **Made false by this PR**, on the same grounds. NEW: "A detail two levels below its root master is answered the same way: its write is admitted exactly when the caller holds the verb on the detail and may update the middle master directly, which also needs edit access to the root, and refused otherwise, so the family reports such a chain `proven`." **Truthful on this head**, on the same grounds; it reads correctly in its paragraph (after the unattributed-refusal and system-door sentences, before the exit-code paragraph, which still names `contradicted` / `failed` as the family's failures). No separate `@objectstack/verify` changeset is owed for this line: it documents the still-pending `--parent-write-reach` family, whose own release note is the corrected 15953 entry, shipping in the same release. Confirmed.
- **`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, the twin.** OLD: "Today's engine refuses every write to a detail two levels below its root master (a line under a quote under an account), even where the caller edits the middle master, so an app that declares such a chain fails the run." **Made false by this PR**, on the same grounds. NEW: "A detail two levels below its root master (a line under a quote under an account) is answered the same way: its write is admitted exactly when the caller holds the verb on the detail and may update the middle master directly, which also needs edit access to the root, and refused otherwise, so such a chain is reported proven." **Truthful on this head**, and consistent with the paragraph's earlier sentence that the master-edit half is measured "by an empty update of the master as the caller, which runs every write gate the master has — for a master that is itself controlled by its parent, the gate above it too". Build Docs, Check Documentation Links and the docs & code guards are green on the head. Confirmed.

None of the three new sentences carries a tracker number, and none claims more than the engine does at this head.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23093-cbp-middle-master-floor.md` declares `@objectstack/plugin-security: patch`, carries `Clause-②: no` in its body, and the PR body's line reads `Clause-②: no — a runtime authorization behaviour under the maintainer's ruling A; no published accept set or public surface moves.` This matches what the diff publishes: a fix in a released package that moves no public surface and no accept set is `patch` (the level follows the act; no `index`, key or value widened), the director binding itself prescribes "a patch changeset", and the nearest precedent — commit 498f4e884, leg 1's floor drop at this same leg — took `patch`. Not breaking: no key or export is removed, so no migration text and no ADR-0087 marker is owed, and the ADR-0087 step passed on the head. The body states for upgraders the admitted class, the still-refused classes, the one narrowing ("Also refused now") and the unchanged classes — an adequate release note. `@objectstack/verify` and `@objectstack/cli` release nothing of their own here beyond the pending 15953 note, corrected above; no `skip-changeset`. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev report 6133252394 (round 3).** Open question (extend the 2026-08-15 ruling to the hop: A / B / C) → ruled A at 6133922339, bound at 6134050293. Out-of-scope 1 (the card's grade rested on a regression that was not one) → triage re-graded at 6133394280: p1 stays, `target:v18` off. All answered.
- **Dev report 6136047254 (patch round).** No open questions. Its gate reading (96 run, only `check-empty-changeset` red) agrees with the check-runs on the head.

- **Fork clause (6134050293).** No case at either layer where a line write is admitted while the same principal's direct middle-master update is refused: the pin file asserts the pair in every case, the dev reports none, and none is visible in the diff.
